transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Anika Shah (Redwood Product); Jared Kim (CTO, ClearVoice), Lina Torres (SRE), Priya Nair (Eng Manager), Sam Ortiz (Data Scientist)

Summary: High-level migration demo focused on API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood; console tour (routes, model catalog), Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, and security discussion (VPC, KMS, audit logs). Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for cost/latency and needs pilot/test plan.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um Jared thanks for the intros. we'll do a quick 30 minute demo and then leave 15ish for Q&A and next steps.
[00:28] Jared: cool yea thanks, we're excited to see parity mapping because we've got a couple services running on OpenAI right now and an internal experiment with Anthropic and Together models with different latency profiles.
[01:05] Marcus: awesome, i'll kick it off with the API mapping slide — basically two goals today: show the 1-to-1 call equivalence (request/response, streaming, function calls) and then the console + optimize features that reduce cost. fair?
[01:42] Priya: yes, and prioritize the parts about our inference costs — we saw token cost spikes on long conversations.
[02:10] Marcus: right — so first, API parity. Redwood exposes a simple REST/SDK, our parameters map pretty directly: prompt -> input, max_tokens -> max_output_tokens, temperature/top_p the same. note: function calling we support but internal naming's slightly different — we call it "tool call" in the console sometimes so sorry if that shows up in docs.
[02:48] Sam: do you also map streaming endpoints? we rely on streaming for live chat.
[03:12] Marcus: yep, streaming is full supported, same chunked deltas, we also support structured output and can stream JSON in pieces — small caveat is we have slightly different SSE event names in our SDK vs OpenAI which is trivial in code.
[04:05] Lina: can you talk about KV cache, i think you said "KV cache" — how does that work across sessions?
[04:28] Marcus: yep it's our prefix / kv cache, sometimes the docs call it KV cache or KV cash in older notes so watch out for typos, it keeps the key value cache on the runtime so repeated prompts avoid re-evaluating the same tokens and that saves cost. for private deployments it stays in-memory on the node unless you enable shared cache.
[05:03] Jared: ok sounds good. what about model mapping — we have some calls to gpt-4 style and some to Claude 3/Anthropic. is there a recommended equivalent?
[05:24] Marcus: we maintain a model catalog. for example: gpt-4 family maps to redwood-4h/4o (performance variants), Claude 3 maps to redwood-c3, and Together models map to redwood-together-compat. each catalog entry has perf profiles (latency/cost for common seq lengths). we will send the link to the catalog after.
[06:10] Priya: when you say "redwood-4h" is that hosted or do we need dedicated?
[06:25] Anika: those are model variants available across both Hosted and Dedicated; you can pin variants in Dedicated for consistent perf. Hosted will route to the best current variant in-region.
[07:00] Jared: we've had issues with small p95 latency spikes on marketplace models, does Redwood do fallbacks automatically?
[07:22] Marcus: yes, smart routing — policy based routing by latency/cost/region, and can fallback to a compatible variant. e.g., if 4h isn't available we fallback to 4o or a quantized variant. we also have graceful degradation that preserves streaming.
[08:05] Sam: curious about embeddings — we're moving some retrieval to embeddings too. do you support the same vector dims?
[08:26] Marcus: embeddings are supported; dims depend on model family, but we provide a mapping table. we'll share a small CSV mapping dims and sample code.
[09:00] Sofia: switching gears to the Console — i'll share screen and walk through routes, cost breakdowns, and the Optimize suggestions.
[09:24] [screen share noise] Sofia: here is the model catalog, search, and perf profiles — notice the cost per token estimate and p50/p95 latencies. you can create a route that maps an external endpoint to a model/version and attach policies for batching and caching.
[10:10] Priya: can we set route-level token limits and per-tenant quotas?
[10:27] Sofia: yes, quotas, rate-limits, and token caps per key; also routing rules so you can route high-value customers to Dedicated.
[11:00] Sofia: Optimize section — this is where we auto-suggest batching windows, cache prefixes, and quantization profiles. in your case with mixed short/long conversations we recommend adaptive batching with a 20ms window for short chat and larger windows for bulk scoring.
[11:40] Sam: what about quantization impacts on quality — we've seen hallucinations go up when we switch to 4-bit.
[11:55] Anika: we run quality evals tied to prompt sets, and Optimize links regressions to score deltas. we recommend running a small eval on a holdout prompt set during the pilot.
[12:24] Jared: security — we need VPC, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and SOC2.
[12:42] Sofia: yes we support private deployments with customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations, VPC peering, and full audit logs. we'll attach the security pack. quick note: some early docs reference "Redwood Dedication" — that's a doc typo for "Redwood Dedicated" sorry.
[13:15] Lina: for VPC do you allow egress control to block model downloads? we have strict policies.
[13:34] Marcus: for on-prem and private we can restrict egress; for Hosted we support VPC peering and strict egress rules via NAT/gw setups — we'll want your network team to share a diagram.
[14:05] Priya: how long to get a Dedicated cluster up? we've got timelines for Q3 pilot.
[14:22] Anika: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks after contract for a basic Dedicated pool, shorter if we reuse standard configs; for Private/on-prem it varies more.
[14:50] Sam: run us through an example migration snippet — a simple replacement of an OpenAI call to Redwood.
[15:06] Marcus: sure. example: curl to OpenAI with authorization header becomes curl to api.redwood.ai/v1/generate, body fields map prompt->input, model->model, you can enable streaming by adding ?stream=true. i'll paste a sample gist after the call.
[16:00] [murmur] Jared: any compatibility libraries for Together/Anthropic?
[16:18] Marcus: we have thin adapters and SDK helpers — Together's auth is slightly different but the adapter handles mapping of generation params. edge-case: function-calling for Anthropic had different schema keys, we remap automatically but test your tooling.
[17:05] Lina: cost comparison question — can you give a quick example of typical token cost delta?
[17:22] Marcus: rough example: at high token volumes our deduping, caching, and batching can yield 20-40% lower per-token cost vs raw hosted marketplace calls; Dedicated often brings further gains depending on utilization. we'll run an apples-to-apples benchmark with your sample traffic.
[18:10] Priya: SLA and uptime — what's included?
[18:27] Sofia: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Hosted has best-effort with credits for major incidents. enterprise packages include higher retention for logs and advanced SLAs.
[19:00] Jared: any gotchas we should know for session state or streaming when switching?
[19:18] Marcus: session state is preserved if you keep the same conversation ids and pass that through; KV cache behavior can differ across runtime versions so we recommend test runs. also watch for SSE event name differences I mentioned earlier.
[20:10] Sam: how do we measure quality regression post-migration?
[20:26] Anika: we instrument evals: baseline on your prompt set, then post-migration compare thresholds, and Optimize alerts on regression. you can schedule automated runs as part of your CI.
[21:05] [phone notification sound] 
[21:30] Priya: ok good — i'd like to make sure we get a scoped POC with clearly defined success metrics: latency p95 under X, cost per 1M tokens under Y, and quality score >= 95 on eval set.
[22:00] Marcus: yes we'll help define those metrics; typical POC includes a 2-week bench with 3-5k sample prompts.
[23:10] Jared: on billing model, do you support monthly committed usage for Dedicated and usage-based for Hosted?
[23:28] Sofia: yes committed monthly/annual for Dedicated; Hosted is pay-as-you-go with optional reserved capacity blocks.
[24:05] Sam: any internal references or shared docs for migration?
[24:18] Sofia: we'll send a migration checklist, a mapping spreadsheet, the security pack, and sample SDK snippets. links: deck: https://redwood.ai/deck/migration-overview, security: https://redwood.ai/security-pack, repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/migration-examples
[25:00] Priya: are there cases you recommend not migrating (i.e., models tied to proprietary infra)?
[25:20] Marcus: if you rely on very specific proprietary models with private weights only on marketplace, that can be tricky; otherwise most generative workloads map cleanly.
[26:00] [long pause, typing]
[27:10] Marcus: quick demo of the console route creation — you choose model, attach batching policy, and choose quota. watch the cost estimator updating in real time.
[28:05] Sofia: now Optimize runbook — it flagged two suggestions for you: reduce 4-bit quantization on conversational models and enable prefix caching for your frequent prompts. we included expected cost delta in the suggestion.
[29:30] Jared: how do we do canary rollouts? can we route a % of traffic to Redwood Dedicated while keeping majority on OpenAI?
[29:50] Sofia: yes; we support weight-based routing and A/B policies so you can split traffic by percentage or by customer key.
[30:45] Priya: about data retention, can we set per-route retention or auto-delete?
[31:05] Marcus: yes configurable retention per route, plus options to disable retention entirely for sensitive workloads.
[31:50] Sam: for the POC, how do we validate token accounting? we want to ensure cost reporting matches our expectations.
[32:10] Marcus: Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-request traces; we also provide logs you can export to S3 for offline reconciliation.
[33:00] Priya: are there any dependencies on providers we should be aware of?
[33:18] Anika: Hosted uses cloud GPUs; Dedicated can be in your cloud account or ours depending on contract; for Private/on-prem we work with your infra teams.
[34:05] Jared: timeline sync — we want to start a pilot early September. can Redwood commit to a 2-week benchmark and then a 4-week pilot?
[34:22] Sofia: yes that's reasonable; we'll propose dates in the follow-up.
[35:00] [muted background]
[36:10] Marcus: demo wrap — i'll drop a sample SDK mapping in the repo, and we'll run an initial smoke test once you share sample prompts.
[36:45] Priya: ok good. Lina any security concerns to flag now?
[37:02] Lina: mainly KMS vendor compatibility and egress control; also we'd like more detail on audit log retention and who's got access.
[37:25] Sofia: we'll include a section in the security pack detailing KMS integrations (AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault) and how audit logs are scoped.
[38:10] Sam: on the quality side, can you support a scoring rubric for our evals?
[38:28] Anika: yes, we can help build a rubric and run evals; Optimize will surface regressions and historical deltas.
[39:00] Jared: any references for prior migrations from Together?
[39:18] Marcus: we did a migration with a mid-market SaaS and observed a 28% cost reduction after batching and caching tweaks; i'll anonymize and send the benchmark.
[40:05] Priya: ok we need a clear owner for the pilot internally — I'll nominate Priya as PM and Jared as exec sponsor.
[40:22] Priya: happy to own.
[41:00] [brief sidebar about pricing tiers]
[42:10] Sofia: recap: we'll send pricing + dedicated worksheet, migration checklist, security pack, mapping spreadsheet, and schedule POC scoping. Redwood will run an initial smoke parity test once ClearVoice sends sample prompts.
[42:40] Marcus: action items: I'll run the quick parity tests; Sofia will send security + pricing; ClearVoice to share traffic.
[43:10] Jared: sounds great thanks everyone.
[43:40] [wrap up small talk]
[44:00] Meeting end

Recap/Next steps: 1) Redwood to share security pack, mapping sheet, pricing (Sofia) 2) Redwood SE to run smoke parity tests and bench with sample prompts (Marcus) 3) ClearVoice to share sample prompt set and traffic profile (Jared/Lina) 4) Schedule POC scoping call for early next week.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional misattributions and minor transcription typos (e.g., "KV cash"), proper nouns may be slightly off.
